24.title: Hamster Scouts Missive 3
24.content:
Dear friend,

Long time no see!

Witty and I asked to be dispatched to the Wilder's territory, but she ended up in the Shimmerwood and I got sent to Vaduso Mountains! Captain Chippy's got some nerve, huh? Anyways, I'm glad I got sent here, because I wouldn't have learned about the Lover's Forest otherwise! They say that if you get married in this sea of pink flowers, a goddess will bless your wedding! I definitely have to bring Witty here next time!

The Wilder here basically live off of Twilight Tree fruits. They taste fine, but acorns are way better! They don't seem too fond of outsiders, either; it always feels like we're bothering them. Still, this isn't a problem for an ace scout like me! I found a whole field of medicinal herbs out here, and while the Wilder usually only trade with their own kind... I managed to work out a little deal with them! Am I awesome or what?!

I also met a Wilder kid out here. He's clearly younger than me, but keeps acting like he's my older sibling! Annoying, right? He's just taller than me, that's all! Anyways, he showed me the mushroom treehouse where he used to take classes, as well as his secret base in the forest... He didn't say so, but I can tell that he really wants to go back to his studies. Unfortunately, his folks are too scared of the monsters around here to let him go.

But they have nothing to worry about, now that you chased the monsters off! I'll tell him first thing tomorrow!

—Hallie

142.title: Leafy Letter
142.content:
Dear Magister,

How have you been lately? Is your journey still going well?

A few days ago, Florabelle took me to the academy to spend time with the younger kids. There were so many classmates, all excited. I was a bit nervous, but Florabelle comforted me and suggested I share some tales of the great Magister Merlin.

So, I shared the experience at Lovers' Wish. Strangely, as I kept talking, I stopped feeling anxious. We talked a lot, enjoyed delicious food, and laughed together under the leaves for a long time... It was wonderful.

Such a joyous experience must also be a blessing brought on by your magic.

Enclosed with the letter are the flowers I recently picked. I wish you a wonderful journey!

143.title: Dusty Letter
143.content:
Magister!

The desert is buzzing with excitement these days! It's not like the Warsong Festival, but a special celebration just for the little ones to enjoy! I took the kids from the clan along and they had an incredible time!

Lumont has drawn many pictures for us, including one just for you! The children also wanted to give you some gifts, so we've included them with this letter! Can you guess which one is from me?

Wishing you a fun and safe journey!
143.sender:
With love, Alsa!
& Everyone of the Uru Clan!

144.title: Elegant Missive
144.content:
Dear Magister,

It's been a while, is your journey going well?

I'm also on a journey of my own. Recently, I visited a town that was having an early summer festival. I planned to set up a booth, but the locals roped me into all sorts of strange activities, leaving me feeling disoriented.

Later, I found out that the festival was specifically for children to enjoy. I never expected that after traveling for so long, I would be treated like a child... It was a somewhat amusing and bewildering experience.

Enclosed with this letter are a few trinkets, nothing of great value, but they make for a pleasant pastime during leisure moments.

145.title: Letter From Marilee
145.content:
Hey Magister!

Recently, the mountains near the ruins have been bustling, and business is booming. It was perfect timing for a rare festival, and I spent the whole day playing with my younger siblings. I was supposed to be responsible but got carried away, and we went home late and got scolded by our grandparents.

It's been a long time since I did something so childish, but, between you and me, I had an incredibly fun time.

How have you been lately? If you have the time, why not go join the festival and have some fun?

Enclosed are some homemade treats from Grandma. Wishing you safe travels and all the happiness in the world!

146.title: My New Discovery!
146.content:
Magister, it's Damian! I've made a stupendous discovery!

Attending lively festivals, eating delicious food, playing games, and performing with my little chariot and airplane is so much fun! It's like the excitement of inventing something amazing!

However, when I try to explain this to others, they just can't seem to understand... but then I thought of you. You're always busy saving the world and studying magic. So, you must understand just how amazing my new discovery is, right?

This is the gift I brought back from the celebration to share with you!

147.title: Tattered Letter
147.content:
I ate something sweet, sweeter than honey! Patto had some and loved it too!

Here are me and Patto's spoils! They were so sweet and yummy that we had to share some with you!

Eat big, grow big, and stay happy!

148.title: Warm Greetings
148.content:
Hello Magister,

Are you still continuing your journey?

Many children grow up listening to the legendary stories of the great Merlin, and I am no exception. So, to have the privilege of witnessing firsthand the brand new legend you have created and sharing it with the children of the next generation as a teacher is an incredibly surreal experience for me.

As your journey progresses, children across the continent will surely hear more legends about Merlin, and there will definitely be people like me who will continue to tell your stories. I know the future will be full of excitement.

During the festival, I made small gifts with the children and sent them with this letter. We wish you a smooth journey.
148.sender:
Florabelle
& Students of the Jade Lake Academy

196.title: Here's the treasure I owe you!

Hey there, Merlin!

Our latest adventure on Dream Isle was simply thrilling! When Grandpa Ulmus woke up, I told him everything that happened. He laughed at our antics and praised our courage and cleverness. It was such a delight! We haven't chatted so much in ages, and Grandpa Ulmus even said I've become as chirpy as a cheerful little sparrow!
    
By the way... I know I promised to send you some of my treasures, but wouldn't you know it, my prettiest dresses were whisked away by Grandpa Ulmus' squirrels to make their nests! To make it up to you, I rummaged through my chest of wonders and found other trinkets. 

I also want to mention that packing them all up and sending to you was no small feat! Enclosed with this letter are also some of my favorite flowers. May they forever bring you sweet dreams.
    
And another thing, remember to sleep well. I'll visit you in your dreams!

334.title: Atalanta's Letter
334.content:
Hey there! Whether it's day or night, I hope this letter finds you in high spirits!
You're probably wondering what's got me in such a cheerful mood, and let me tell you, I've been feeling fantastic lately!

Just a few days ago, some scholars from the Evergreen Conservatory came to me with a super fun request! They needed a brave explorer (that's me!) to help explore a mysterious ruin filled with fascinating arcane symbols and tricky traps. They insisted that only someone as skilled as I could take on such a challenge!

Of course, Temesia didn't approve at first, but once I zipped through every challenge and won the scholars' endless thanks, even she had to give me a little nod of approval!

Tonight, they're throwing a bonfire to celebrate our successful adventure and honor my contributions. I'll be showing off my grilling skills, I just know it's going to be a blast. I really wish you could join the fun!

Oh! And even though I said I'd hang up my treasure-thieving hat, I couldn't resist snagging a few ancient inscriptions just for you. I remember you mages can use them to <style="highlight">redeem rewards</style>!

Don't say I never did you any favors! I've jotted it down below, make sure to put it to good use!



Wishing you safe travels!

<align="right">Yours adventurously,
<align="right">Atalanta
<align="right">The World's Greatest Treasure Hunter

335.title: Letter from Traveler's Light
335.content:
Dear Magister,

I just finished the outpost errand the General assigned to me, and I hear you've already spirited yourself away!

Things here have become almost too quiet, you know. No fresh tales at the tavern, and the place has gone stale without your antics and the endless chatter of those two hamsters. One might almost say I miss it.

The General mentioned a holiday for you in Cedartown, yet the Solitaries there haven't heard a peep from you! I suspect you've found yourself another one of those serendipitous adventures. Well, next time, let's make sure I'm there with you! I'll even get the General's permission for an extended leave. Not to shirk duties, of course, but purely in the interest of companionship.

Until then, I'll save a seat for you at the Traveler's Light for a proper catch-up. And naturally, the tab will still be on the General!

<align="right">Your devoted knight,
<align="right">Valen

336.title: Letter That Smells Like BBQ
336.content:
It's been a while!

The little Maulers won't stop begging for more of your adventure stories! I've told them all the ones I know a hundred times, they've practically memorized them. Soren even bought a storybook from a merchant to keep them busy. It's called "Mermaid in the Sea" and now they're asking a million new questions!

Like, "What's the sea? What's a mermaid? Why don't we have mermaids in the desert? Has Magister Merlin ever seen one?" I was stumped! Soren finally told them, "If you grow up and become as skilled as the magister, you can go see for yourselves if there are mermaids in the sea." Not bad, right?

Anyway, where are you off to now? Everyone here misses you tons! We sent a small gift with this letter. Make sure you eat well, sleep well, and come back soon for some roast meat!

<align="right">Alsa and Soren
<align="right">And all your friends in the Uru Clan

337.title: Neatly Written Letter
337.content:
Dear Magister,

This is my very first letter, sent under the name "Lily May". I've asked one of the acolytes to help me write this.

Lately, letters have arrived from many people—Granny Dahnie, Lenya, and a few teachers from the Jade Lake Academy. The acolytes at the temple read them aloud to me. I've learned so much from them... about the world, and the things I did that hurt people, things I didn't fully understand at the time.

I never thought much of letters before, but now... they feel like a gift. Once, I wouldn't have dared to write one myself. But a voice inside me kept saying, "Try it." And so, I thought of you.

I hear you're traveling by the sea... My people used to move with the seasons. I wonder, is that a kind of "travel" too? As for the future, I haven't thought too much beyond finding my mother. Perhaps this letter will be my own small beginning.

I hope next time, I can write you a letter without anyone else's help.

<align="right">Best,
<align="right">Lily May

340.title: Letter from Hogan
340.content:
Old friend, it's been far too long since we last exchanged words. How fares your journey?

Have you reached Cedartown, or perhaps fate has guided you to new adventures, adding another remarkable chapter to the chronicles of Merlin's illustrious exploits? Whatever your path, I hope you'll find time to write to me when you can.

The air has turned crisp here in Holistone with the approach of the <style="highlight">Winter Carnival</style>. It's the season of snow and gatherings. The town has grown lively as merchants arrive in greater numbers. Thanks to you, Ryeham's bountiful wheat harvest has found eager buyers. Both the village chief and the Mithril Consortium send their gratitude. Judging by the recent shipment records, their <style="highlight">festival banquet</style> promises to surpass all expectations this year.

If your travels bring you back this way during the <style="highlight">festival season</style>, I eagerly await the chance to welcome you again. It would bring me great joy to share a toast and recount the incredible stories of our time apart.

P.S. Valen recently stumbled upon an old manuscript, and upon closer examination, it appears to contain the ancient runes you once mentioned—used for conjuring rewards from thin air. He was adamant that I send it to you, so I have copied it below. I hope it will serve you well on your journey.



Wishing you:
<align="right">Good health
<align="right">Yours faithfully,
<align="right">Hogan

341.title: Dreamy Letter
341.content:
Hello, <style="stress"><player_name></style>! How are you? Have you had any interesting dreams lately?

Life here has been as delightful as ever. Dreams are such curious things, aren't they? One moment, they're vivid as a painted sky, and the next, they flit away like a mischievous breeze—here and gone, yet somehow forever etched in the heart. Truly marvelous, wouldn't you agree?

But ah, reality has its own clock. Another year has nearly ended, and a new one is just around the corner.

Your adventures this past year must have been simply magical! Everywhere I flutter, I hear whispers of Merlin's deeds rekindling the sparks of wonder in people's hearts. You've reminded many to chase their dreams again and even helped some achieve them!

You know, you have this way of turning the forgotten into the unforgettable. That's just who you are, Magister Merlin, always bringing us miracles!

So, here's my wish for the new year: let's gather fresh dreams and make them soar higher than ever!

Oh, oh! Before I forget, I stumbled upon a tiny treasure while skipping through the dreamworld. It's one of those ancient runes left by the wizards of yore, meant for <style="highlight">trading shiny rewards</style>! I've scribbled it down below.



Wishing you:
<align="right">Dreams as dazzling as the stars!
<align="right">Your eternal friend,

Dear Merlin, how have you been? I trust that no matter where you are, your light is brightening the days of those around you, even under the gloomiest skies.

The <style="highlight">Emberlight Festival</style> is almost here! It's my favorite time of year—brimming with warmth, joy, and the magic of togetherness. When that time comes, as I soar through the night sky, the streams of light will dance around me, making even my feathers a part of the dazzling display.

So, <style="stress"><player_name></style>, when will you return to Holistone? I've been counting down the days, waiting for us to celebrate the festival together. <align="right">Talene

358.title: Valka's Letter
358.content:
<style="stress"><player_name></style>, it has been a few days since we parted, yet the thought of your current endeavors lingers in my mind. What calls your attention these days?

The Snowspire Festival in Cedartown has come to an end, though the spirit of the Emberlight Festival still lingers in the frosty air. Cedartown, nestled at the base of the towering white peaks, stays true to its traditions. Fireworks are only allowed on festival nights and in carefully chosen areas to keep everyone safe in these rugged lands.

Some visiting merchants have grumbled that these rules take away some of the fun, but I'd argue that Whiteridge has its own unique charm.

Instead of fireworks, lanterns take the spotlight. Snow sculptures stand like quiet sentinels, and ice lanterns glow with unmatched brilliance. Just a few days ago, I walked through the streets and couldn't help but marvel at how the town felt like something out of a dream—vivid lights and untouched snow blending into a magical scene.

I overheard someone asking if such beauty came from magic, alchemy, or maybe even dwarven handiwork. The question piqued my curiosity, but I quickly realized it's a mystery for someone with a sharper mind than mine. Perhaps when you visit, you'll uncover the answer I couldn't find.

<style="stress"><player_name></style>, my friend, I hope we can walk these streets together someday. The snow and lanterns would be even more magical with you here, and I'm certain Cedartown's famous desserts would taste better in your company. If you arrived now, I'm sure the innkeeper of the Frozen Paw would welcome you with a feast!

I'm sending along an ancient rune I recently found. I've heard mages use relics like this to <style="highlight">earn great rewards</style>, so I hope it proves useful.



Wishing you:
<align="right">Safe travels and good health
<align="right">Always your loyal ally,
<align="right">Valka

359.title: Lyca's Invitation
359.content:
It's been a while, <style="stress"><player_name></style>. How has your journey been? Though we haven't exchanged letters in some time, your name keeps finding its way to me. Travelers and merchants speak of your incredible deeds, and even the winds seem eager to carry your stories far and wide.

It's still a bit chilly here in the Vaduso Mountains, but spring is creeping in. The land is slowly turning a vibrant green, almost as if touched by magic—perhaps it's Misarte's blessing or just the quiet wonder of spring's arrival.

The Lovers' Wish flowers have bloomed in full splendor, painting the valleys with delicate colors. Though flowers bloom here year-round, there's something special about these early spring blossoms. An old poem once said Lovers' Wish flowers shine brightest at winter's end, as if welcoming spring. Maybe that's why so many visitors have come—locals from the Dark Forest and even Lightbearer travelers. And yet, amidst all the chatter, your name comes up again and again. It reminded me how much I miss you and inspired me to send this invitation.

If you have the time, come see this breathtaking sea of flowers. Parisa, Florabelle, and even Bryon. We're all eager to see you again. I know this place will feel even more beautiful with you here.

Oh, and I found something curious while flipping through an old poetry collection. Florabelle says it's something mages can use to <style="highlight">obtain rewards</style>. I've transcribed it for you in case it might be useful!



Wishing you safe travels
<align="right">And hoping we'll see each other soon,

368.title: Letter From Valen
368.content:
<style="stress"><player_name></style>, how's life treating you lately?

We've handled our duties quite well these past few days. The chill in the air shows no sign of letting up, and it seems even bandits and merchants have decided to hunker down by their hearths. For once, the Heroic Order has been granted a rare and much-needed respite from the chaos.

Not that peace and quiet isn't nice. It's just that after a while, it starts to feel a bit boring... or maybe lonely?

Then again, I doubt you'd understand that feeling. You, our oh-so-mighty mage, are always out and about on some marvelous adventure, right? Yep, that was a jab, and yeah, I'm griping that you never thought about inviting your loyal knight along. Next time you try sneaking off without me, I'm coming after you!	

Anyway, since we were bored, or lonely, for that matter, we decided to hold a small spring fair in Holistone. Sure, it's the earliest of early spring, but everyone jumped at the chance to ditch their heavy clothes. Half of them ended up catching colds. But if you ask me, totally worth it! The vibe was so festive it felt like spring had already arrived.

I've enclosed a few little keepsakes from the fair. Hope you like them. And hey, if you get the chance, go out and enjoy the weather. It's just about perfect right now.

<align="right">Feeling a bit under the weather,
<align="right">Valen

369.title: Mikola's Warm Invitation
369.content:
<style="stress"><player_name></style>, it's been so long!
Winter's finally behind us, and spring is on its way! Sure, it's always hot around here, but every season has its own kind of heat! Right now, it's the kind that wakes you up and gets you moving!

That's right, we're holding another ball! This one's to celebrate the first flower blooming on Mars Peak. It's a sign that spring's almost here, and what better time for everyone to gather and have some fun?

By day, we'll be sparring, because what are the Maulers without a good old-fashioned tournament? It's in our blood, after all! And when night falls, the real party begins. Remember those fireworks you made for the Emberlight Festival? People loved them so much we couldn't resist giving them a twist. Now, they bloom into dazzling flowers across the night sky. With songs, dancing, and bonfires blazing, it feels like even spring itself has joined the celebration!

I've enclosed a few little keepsakes from the festivities! If you've got the chance, come and see it for yourself!

<align="right">Forever passionate,
<align="right">Mikola

370.title: Letter from Dionel
370.content:
My dear <style="stress"><player_name></style>, how have you been these days? Any delightful tales to share from the lands of fun and frolic?

I'll be honest, I've been a bit bored—can you believe it? You know that in-between time, when winter's leaving but spring's not quite ready to take its place? It's the worst for throwing a proper bash. You can't have a snow-viewing gathering without snow, and you can't enjoy flower-viewing without flowers. The wine in the cellar is still aging, and the best seasonal dishes are stuck in the realm of ideas, waiting for the right ingredients. Even if I do manage to scrape together something festive, the weather scares off half the guests. And when I try to invite a few bards to liven things up, they just shrug and say there's nothing worth singing about.

But finally, those dreary days are over! Buds are blooming, fresh green shoots are everywhere, and the sun's getting warmer with each passing day. It's the perfect time to slip into something new, laugh till your cheeks hurt at a fair, and raise a glass to the season of new beginnings!

That's exactly what I've been doing. And to bring a little joy your way, I've enclosed a few gifts. If they lift your spirits, all the better.

<align="right">Dionel

371.title: Letter from Carolina
371.content:
<style="stress"><player_name></style>, it's been a while.

For me, most days felt like a long, quiet winter. The soft fall of snow and the occasional crack of a breaking branch were the only sounds in the silence. Those moments were like tiny surprises—my own kind of melodies, if you will.

I used to love watching the flicker of a candle, how those tiny flames could make forgotten, dusty corners glow like they were gilded. To me, it felt like the closest thing to sunlight.

But then you came along, and for the first time, I saw what dawn really looks like. Valka told me that in Cedartown, people are laughing and singing, having the time of their lives. And that the sun is warm, the grass is starting to grow, and the flower fields are more gorgeous than ever. Everyone's out in the great outdoors enjoying this divine gift that is spring.

For someone like me, who's only ever known winters, this spring opens up a whole new world for me. I've enclosed a small gift I picked up during one of these newfound moments of joy. I hope it carries some of this wonder and warmth your way.

May your journeys be safe.


<align="right">Yours faithfully,
<align="right">Carolina

372.title: Message from Odie
372.content:
It's been a while! How's life been treating you?

Business has been good lately, so I figured it was time for a little break. This time of year is perfect, isn't it? The weather's neither too hot nor too dry, and for once, I don't feel buried under a mountain of work. What little I have to do, I can manage at my own pace.

Because of that, I think, I'm seeing a lot more folks just taking it easy on the road. Not that they're lazing around in a bad way. It's just that no one's spoiling for a fight at the drop of a hat anymore. Granted, bounty-hunting jobs are still going on daily, but everyone seems more laid-back about it.

Right now, for example, I'm watching young couples strolling hand in hand, back and forth along the street like they've got all the time in the world. You know what I'm talking about! Just sitting here and watching them brings peace to my mind.

I've enclosed some tasty little snacks I found, perfect with a cup of tea. If you've got some free time, why not swing by Alkali and lounge in the sun with me for a bit?

<align="right">All the best!
<align="right">Odie

373.title: Letter From Parisa
373.content:
<style="stress"><player_name></style>, it's been a while.

How goes your journey? Discovered anything interesting lately?
Right now, I'm writing to you from under the shade of the Lucent Tree.

This gorgeous giant still lazily stretches its branches like it always does, and the Dark Forest is as cozy and calm as ever. It's probably because spring is almost here, but we've been getting a bit more rain. The weather hasn't cooled off, though—everything feels softly wrapped in a warm haze. The raindrops glisten on the Lucent Tree's leaves, making the light appear all dreamy, like something out of a fairy tale. Lyca and Florabelle were saying how the tree looks even more romantic now.

And I'd have to agree. Lately, this place has become a favorite for dates. Even Lovers' Wish pales in comparison. After all, Lovers' Wish won't be in full bloom for another month, and there's something uniquely magical about the fleeting, rain-kissed early spring view here.

What about you? What views are you feasting your eyes on right now? I bet they're nothing short of spectacular, too. If you have the time, maybe you'd like to drop by and see the Lucent Tree for yourself?

I've enclosed our newest blend of herbal tea. May it brighten your spirits.

<align="right">Parisa

374.title: Greetings From Mirael
374.content:
<style="stress"><player_name></style>, it's been a while.

How are things on your end? Discovered any uncharted lands lately? Even if you don't send word, word of your exploits always finds its way to me. After all, the passing merchants never miss a chance to spin tales of Merlin, the legendary mage. Your adventures are like rare treasures in this otherwise ordinary world. Everybody hungers for a taste of the extraordinary, and you never fail to deliver.

But as much as I enjoy hearing secondhand tales, nothing compares to hearing them directly from you or, better yet, witnessing them myself. Surely, as your student, I've earned that small privilege, haven't I?	

The last time we shared a meal was during the Winter Carnival. I still take out the flower you gave me to admire it. And today, as luck would have it, I wandered to our old meeting spot in Holistone and found flowers already blooming.

That's when it dawned on me: spring is quietly on its way.

And it's been nearly two months since we last met.

Even as I put pen to paper, I can't tell which I feel more strongly: the joy of seeing spring's arrival, or the ache of missing you. If anyone has the answer, it's you, my all-knowing teacher.

I've enclosed a few small gifts. I hope that by the time spring comes in its full glory, we can meet here once again. I'll show you the very first flower that bloomed.

<align="right">Your forever companion and student,
<align="right">Mirael

395.title: Sealed Letter
395.content:
Dear Magister,
 
I hope this message finds you well. I apologize for reaching out unexpectedly—may I inquire if you are still in the Duchy of Whiteridge?
 
Since the passing of the Archduke and Princess, Whiteridge has been engulfed in unrest. As the captain of the palace guards, I have done all I can to restore order, but I am uncertain whether all my decisions have been the best for the duchy. In these trying times, you and General Valka remain our last hope. Should you uncover any threat to the duchy or its people, I would be grateful if you would notify me, and I will do everything in my power to investigate.
 
I know that, like General Valka, you are grieving the loss of the princess. While the duchy mourns, <style="highlight">preparations for the funeral are proceeding</style>. Once the unrest has settled, we will hold a grand funeral for the Archduke and the princess, guiding their spirits back to Dura's arms. If you have not left the duchy by then, both the duchy and the Valesa Family would be deeply honored to have you join us in paying tribute to the princess on her final journey.
 
May you remain in good health and travel safely.
<align="right">Yours faithfully,
<align="right">Rodrigo

396.title: Gerda's Message
396.content:
Dear <style="stress"><player_name></style>, how's everything?

The flowers are in bloom, the sun's getting warmer—oh, you know what that means!
Dancing, of course!

Now, don't you go thinking I mean those stiff, proper ballroom affairs. No, no, that's for the nobles and their endless curtsies. Not my style, honey!

Spring is for laughter, good company, and the sweetest treats. When the mood strikes, you just let the music take you—twirling, stomping, singing to your heart's content!

It doesn't matter if you've got two left feet or a voice like a croaking toad—grab your friends and have a ball!
So, it's time to loosen up and have some fun with your friends!

And when you're all danced out, come on over for a warm soak. I'll have something delicious waiting for you.

<align="right">Always ready to be your dance partner,
<align="right">Gerda

397.title: Ludovic's Letter
397.content:
Dear <style="stress"><player_name></style>, it has been some time since I last wrote.

With winter's cruel grasp finally loosening, I find that even the most secluded corners are no longer untouched by laughter and song. The world stirs once more.

For longer than I care to admit, I have embraced silence as my only companion, finding solace in its quiet constancy. And yet, at this time of year, even I must concede—solitude is colder when all else begins to bloom.

Is it the depth of stillness that makes one long for company? Or simply that even the most steadfast grow weary of their own shadows? Whatever the cause, I sense it is time for a change.

I know you value solitude as I do, but surely, one need not revel in grand festivities to enjoy the season. A quiet gathering, a moment shared among familiar faces—such things are enough.

Go on, indulge in the revelry if it pleases you. Should you have need of anything, you know where to find me.

<align="right">Yours faithfully,
<align="right">Ludovic

398.title: Satrana's Invitation
398.content:
Dear <style="stress"><player_name></style>, how's everything?

Still off on some grand adventure, dodging danger and chasing destiny? I know you've got a tale or two up your sleeve!

But that's not why I'm writing—I have something far more important to tell you. It's dancing season again!

I can already see you squinting at this letter, wondering, "Must I really dance?" or perhaps, "Please tell me there won't be another duel." Well... I make no promises!

Spring is all about freedom—no rules, no limits, just the thrill of the moment! A fierce battle or a lively jig? Why not both?

We Maulers don't have any grand festivals ahead, but that doesn't mean we don't know how to celebrate! Instead, we spend time with friends and raise our glasses together, savoring the moment...

If you find yourself with a free moment, come join us! And if you can't, then at least promise me this—wherever you are, celebrate spring with those who make your heart light.

<align="right">Your friend who can't wait to dance,
<align="right">Satrana

403.title: Lorsan's Warm Wishes
403.content:
Feels like we just met yesterday, doesn't it? Though, to be fair, it hasn't been all that long since we last saw each other!

As I said in my last letter, I've started this wild, wonderful new journey—my own little adventure of gathering stories, making friends, and, of course, discovering fantastic food. Why just stick to one thing when you can have it all, right?! So, what about you? Still hanging around Cedartown, or have you already set off on some grand escapade?

You know, it's funny to think back to our very first meeting!
You were just starting to get your memory back, still a bit shaky on the basics of how things worked! Meanwhile, I was charging headfirst into fixing this whole "corruption" mess, fueled by nothing but sheer enthusiasm. That's how I ended up in the vineyards of Ryeham, where I bumped into you and the rest of our ragtag crew.

And what a crew we were! That chance meeting turned into a fresh start for the Dark Forest. Me, my sister, Eironn, Bryon, Parisa—we were all a little lost, but thanks to you, we found our way. Some stayed behind to help the forest thrive, while others set off to explore and grow.
Now, we're all walking our own paths, and I just know we're going to do something amazing someday!

But what I never expected was that our paths would cross again so soon. I can't imagine a better surprise than that!

Anyway, every time I sit down to write, I end up rambling like there's no tomorrow. My sister says my letters are less "letters" and more "stream-of-consciousness chaos." No structure, no fancy phrasing—just me pouring my heart out! But hey, isn't that what letters are for? To say the things you couldn't say in person? What would be the point if I wrote something short and stiff like Bryon's one-liners? My sister, Parisa, and even Eironn take forever to write a letter. They draft outlines, pick the fanciest words, and make it all so formal. Where's the fun in that?

All I'm saying is, this letter is truly from the heart! It's not about showing off my writing skills—though I'll have you know, plenty of people have praised the beauty of my poetry! If you've gotten letters from other people, believe me: if I wanted to, I could outdo all of them and write something far more elegant!

Oh, that reminds me! Have you heard from Gerda? I heard her inn's been having some <style="highlight">strange happenings</style> recently. She's working on it, but I'm a bit worried. If you have a moment, could you <style="highlight">check in on her</style>?

And, while you're at it, could you take a look at the counter? I think I might have left a white wooden box there. It's about the length of my forearm, decorated with a Lucent Tree pattern. Inside you'll find some tuning tools and spare strings cushioned by Elona's feathers. I didn't forget anything, mind you! I double-checked my luggage before leaving! This is just a precaution, just in case it somehow got left behind. For all I know, it could also be sitting in my carriage right now!
Anyway, if you find it, please do let me know!

Oh, and one more thing! I recently came across a new sheet of music and saw a rune that looks familiar. Mages often use it to <style="highlight">claim rewards</style>. I don't need it, so I've copied it down for you. Hopefully, it'll come in handy!

I've got so much more to tell you, but let's save it for the next time we meet. I'm already looking forward to that day!

Until then,
<align="right">I hope you have the most exciting adventures!
<align="right">Your forever best travel buddy (even from afar)
<align="right">and legendary minstrel, Lorsan

<align="left">P.S. I just quickly checked my luggage again and... um, yeah. If you end up stopping by the inn, could you also check the entrance? There's a tiny chance I left my instrument case behind!
And maybe ask Gerda if there's a scarf in the laundry room?

P.P.S. Actually, I think I might have left a couple of my poetry notebooks in my room too. Guess I'll have to go back and look myself. Please disregard the earlier requests. Still, wishing you a safe journey!

P.P.P.S. But hey, if you're still in Cedartown, maybe we'll <style="highlight">run into each other</style> way sooner than expected! Wouldn't that be amazing?!

408.title: Temesia's Memo
408.content:
Dear <style="stress"><player_name></style>, how's everything going on your end?

Time has passed since our last meeting, but I still remember how you resolved the crisis in Whiteridge, and you will always have my gratitude.

My days have been uneventful of late. Upon concluding my duties in Whiteridge, I returned to the temple to attend to the matters that had gathered in my absence. The work proved demanding, yet now that order is restored, Dura has seen fit to grant me an unexpected day of reprieve.

I bring news of Atalanta and Lucius. Atalanta has departed to lend her aid to scholars of the Evergreen Conservatory, while Lucius has returned home to attend to private affairs. And thus, by fate's peculiar design, I find myself alone on this rare day of respite.

Although the endless scrolls and missives left my head all muddled, once I was finally done with all the paperwork, I found myself feeling lost instead of relishing my free time.

Thus, I decided to find something to occupy myself with.

I began by tending to my noble steed, Dawn. She took such delight in her bath that she transformed the stable into something resembling a battlefield. Having restored order to both my mount and the stable, I then turned my attention to the maintenance of our riding equipment. These tasks occupied me until the noon bell, at which point I prepared a humble meal of apple porridge, a fare that pleases both me and my steed alike.

Following lunch, I led Dawn on a leisurely stroll through the township. When we chanced upon a familiar merchant's shop, I bought some sweets that she so favors. The afternoon was pleasant, with the warm breeze brushing against my face, carrying the scent of flowers and fields. As I fed Dawn her treats, I started humming the hymns I learned back in the choir... Time seemed to slow down that day, and all my worries faded away.

Although my quill may lack the grace of a scribe's hand, I beg your patience as I share this humble truth. While our duties may weary the body, they nourish the spirit. For in honest labor, we find purpose, and without it, even the noblest soul grows dull as an unsharpened blade.

Thus, should the hour find you at leisure, embrace some worthy task. You never know what you might discover.

I came across some ancient runes while leafing through a tome. Some told me mages can <style="highlight">earn great rewards</style> from it. I hope it comes in handy for you.

May the Divine Light ever grant you serenity amidst life's storms and stillness alike.

<align="right">Your forever loyal companion,
<align="right">Temesia

409.title: Letter from Sinbad
409.content:
<style="stress"><player_name></style>, bet you can't guess where I am as I write this.

I'm back in Brineville! Surprise! The ladies in the village had been bombarding me with letters while I was away. 'Come back soon, or don't come back at all!' Their threats were scarier than a swarm of starving sharks.

I thought it was about time I went back for a visit anyway, given how long I'd been away.

Whenever I'm home, I can't stop thinking about setting sail for another adventure, but once I'm riding the waves, I find my heart turning toward the shore. Am I starting to lose my adventurous spirit?

As it happens, I went out for a stroll one evening. Bearing gifts, of course. Local delicacies, exotic trinkets, the sort of treasures one collects from distant ports. I left them at the doorsteps of the fair ladies in the village, and what was my reward? Why, they showered me with even greater bounty! Ship's provisions, tinned goods, fine garments! My arms were nearly bursting with the weight of their generosity.

Clearly, everyone in the village kept me in their thoughts while I was away. I have to find a way to repay their kindness.

Wait! I forgot to mention something! Speaking of repaying people's kindnesses. I've got a gift for you as well!

This time, fortune led me to an island so breathtaking it could steal a sailor's heart away. I'm talking about crystal waters, forgotten ruins, and not a soul in sight for leagues. So, naturally, I decided to name it after myself and you, of course, <style="stress"><player_name></style>.

Impressive, right? I've already picked out the perfect spot for you to pitch your tent. Right between the scenic ruins and the best fishing cove. Just try not to keep me waiting too long, or I might claim all the good catches myself.

Also, I came across some ancient runes here. I remember you told me once that runes sometimes <style="highlight">give out rewards</style>. I figured you'd want them so I scribbled them down for you. You're welcome, by the way.


I wish I could tell you more about my voyage, but everyone is calling me to dinner, and trust me, you do not want to keep those ladies waiting! So, I'll have to set down my quill for now. The rest of my tale will have to wait until next time. Don't forget to write me!

<align="right">The greatest captain of the seas and your heart,
<align="right">Sinbad

411.title: Hogan's Letter
411.content:
Dear Magister,
Thanks to you and your familiars, my health has mostly recovered, and I've begun my rehabilitation exercises.

How are things on your side? I just wanted to let you know that I've gone through the report. I know the great Merlin won't be stumped by such minor setbacks, but please bear with me—having lived through the entire ordeal myself, I can't help but feel uneasy at how deliberately understated the report was.

From my investigation, it appears that the royal court has swept the rebellion in Brimstone Village under the rug, and the existence of Sal'thorin and the Essail remains a secret to the public. Apparently, this is the calm before the storm, as the royal court is still assessing the crisis. Once they have the full picture, the storm may well break.

For the royal court, what matters most is the <style="highlight">loyalty</style> of its territories. If that's missing, they should at least offer some <style="highlight">benefit</style> to the empire.

By this measure, I'd say Brimstone Village is now in an extremely precarious position. They can no longer craft their echorite weapons, and the empire has secured other suppliers for underground resources. In other words, with no value and no trust, Brimstone Village holds no meaning for the Lightbearer Empire.

While the empire likely won't punish the innocent villagers, its usual methods suggest they'll scatter the remaining population across distant dwarven settlements—or place them under house arrest. As for Brimstone Village itself, it will most likely be abandoned.

Speaking from an unbiased perspective, I believe it would be a huge waste to simply erase such a historically rich village with outstanding craftsmanship, even though we only got a brief glimpse of it during our visit.

The empire will soon send <style="highlight">an envoy</style> to the village for an inspection.

The arrival of the envoy will be a crisis in itself, but with timely interventions, it could become an opportunity for the village to reverse its fortunes.

I can only bring you up to speed on the current situation in this letter, my old friend. I'm afraid I can't offer you any suggestions or advice at this moment.

I sincerely hope that the famous echorite weapons will be preserved.

All the best!

<align="right">Take care.
<align="right">Yours faithfully,
<align="right">Hogan

413.title: Smokey's Letter
413.content:
Hey there, Magister!
Hope this letter finds you well. The Ashen Wastes hosted a children's festival, and let me tell you, chasing after kids under that desert sun? It's not easy.

But don't worry, we weren't just there to get fleeced at overpriced carnival games. Meerky stumbled upon this wonderfully sweet herb, and we turned it into a cooling brew that sold like wildfire. I swear, if we'd had eight arms each, we still wouldn't have kept up with demand!

Oh, we also ran into a kid selling fake gemstones. He kept insisting his gems were real and even tried to trade them for spices. Meerky climbed up onto his stall, grabbed the biggest "ruby", and smashed it. Guess what? It shattered into dust immediately. We may have, uh, strategically retreated before the kid could recover. After all that excitement, Meerky and I flopped onto the sand, sunbathing while counting our earnings. One part went into savings, another for daily expenses, and another became Meerky's pocket money. Not bad for a day's work!

Oh, and I snagged something you might like during the festival. I found this rune in a dog-eared spellbook that lets mages <style="highlight">claim rewards</style>. Maybe it'll come in handy for you!

That's about all I wanted to say. Next time you're in the area, I'll treat you to one of Meerky's freshly brewed cooling drinks.

<align="right">Yours sincerely, Smokey & Meerky

414.title: Daimon's Letter
414.content:
Hi, <style="stress"><player_name></style>!
It's Daimon! Remember me? I've been the happiest ever since Mom said I can play with the other kids! It's all thanks to you, Mr. Ludovic, and Valka. I'm really grateful to all of you...

Guess what? I made so many new friends! The Flower Attendant and Mister Teapot are really fun. Don't tell them, but I can now run faster than both of them when we play hide-and-seek! Oh, and Carolina and Callan are the best! Carolina has shelves full of books about mages traveling the world. She promised to read them to me whenever I want. But you know what's weird? Some mages don't have fluffy familiars with them on their adventures. How do they not get lonely? Please give Chippy and Hammie a big hug from me. I miss them so much!

Oh right, there's been another big change. Dad used to be so busy, even before... we became Graveborn. After we found each other again, it still felt like his research was more important than me. But after last time, Dad said he wants to spend more time with me too! We even snuck out to the Frozen Paw at night! Dad taught me how to fold towels into ducks and puppies. Stitchy got a bath too! Dad said I can help him design our new house. I'm thinking a cozy fireplace, swinging hammocks, a mini hot spring, and a whole wall just for me to draw on! I want to draw Dad, Mom, me, and all my friends. Of course, I'll also draw you! Dad saw me writing this and asked me to copy down this rune too. He says this lets mages <style="highlight">claim rewards</style>, and that it might help you.

I hope you're having amazing adventures too! When you visit Whiteridge again, I'll show you our new home!

<align="right">Your friend, Daimon

450.title: Marilee's Letter
450.content:
Dear Magister,

It's been a long while since we've had a moon so full. Moonlight is spilling across our little yard tonight, and my younger siblings are laughing and playing in the corner. Grandma just finished baking treats for us... I can already smell them. I wish you were here to try some! The kids are arguing over who got the biggest piece, holding them up and comparing like it's a contest... I'm not sure if any of this sounds interesting to you, but for me, it's these little everyday things that make life feel warm and real.

To be honest, nights like this have been pretty rare in my life. I've been worrying about how to get by for as long as I can remember—and between the bandits, the golems, and all the other messes, things were always chaotic... But ever since we went through that adventure together, everything started to change.

Life has been getting easier, little by little. The village is growing, and there are more smiling faces every day. The kids always have something delicious to eat, and Grandpa and Grandma finally have time to rest. And when I see this? I think of you.

I know you're still off chasing wonders. Even in our little village, and in nearby places like Holistone and Ryeham, I sometimes hear your name drifting through the air in a bard's song.

Recently, while working with the scholars from Evergreen Conservatory, I came across a rune that mages can <style="highlight">draw rewards from</style>. I thought it might be useful to you, so I copied it down and sent it along with the letter—a small token of thanks.

I hope the road ahead treats you kindly, and that wherever you are, the night sky is just as beautiful as it is here.

<align="right">Sincerely,
Marilee

451.title: Lily May's Letter
451.content:
Dear Magister,

Hello! I'm writing this letter from a forest I've never been to before. I've officially set off on my journey to find my mother and the Azure Seers, and I'm resting here for a short while. My handwriting might be a bit shaky... I hope you don't mind.

The people here seem to be celebrating a special occasion. They're busy picking the forest's sweetest, most fragrant fruits, washing them with spring water, and laying them out under the stars. They told me it's a local tradition, a way of honoring the moment when two stars come together in the sky.

Someone gave me a plump, ripe fruit. The moment I held it in my hands, the sweet scent nearly melted my heart.

Is it really such a special thing when two stars meet?

At first, I didn't get it. But then, during the celebration, someone explained it like this: When two stars cross paths, the light they share can help guide people who've been apart back to each other.

That made me stop and think. I saw two faces in my mind—one was my mother's, a little blurry now. The other was yours, bright and clear. And for the first time, I started to understand why everyone was smiling under the stars.

Meeting you felt like that—like a rare and beautiful crossing of stars. A moment I'll always carry with me. As long as that starlight exists, even the darkest night feels a little less lonely.

So even if we're far apart right now, I believe the starlight you once gave me is still out there, still shining. Maybe it's already lighting the path toward our next reunion.

Oh... and a kind villager gave me a small gift. It's said to be a rune that mages can <style="highlight">draw rewards</style> from. I thought of you immediately. I wish I could share the starlight here or the sweetness of that fruit with you, but this will have to do for now. Just a little something to say I'm thinking of you

And if the stars really do bless those who look up at them, then may they guide our journeys, and bring us back together someday.

<align="right">Under the starlight,
Lily May

452.title: Hogan's Message
452.content:
Dear old friend,

You know me, I don't usually write. There's so much I want to say, and it's not easy getting it down on paper. But today, on a whim, I thought I'd tell you how things have been going in Holistone. Funny thing is, the moment I started writing, all I could think about was the time we spent fighting side by side—the battles, the close calls, the adventures. To be honest, it caught me by surprise.

Most of those memories are probably gone from your mind. Ever since you woke up with no recollection of the past, I've never really spoken to you about it. Maybe it's because the moment we met again, when I saw you standing firm in the firelight of Holistone, I knew: Even without your memories, you were still you. Your courage, your kindness—none of that had changed. And neither had the trust between us. That's why I've always believed that no matter what happened, we'd still be the kind of friends who could watch each other's backs.

Since then, you've just kept going. You've taken up the mantle of Merlin, exposed the Adamant Syndicate's schemes, put an end to the corruption in the Dark Forest, and held the line when the golems attacked Holistone... And the further your journey takes you, the more people you end up helping—and I'm one of them.

Just look at what happened in Sal'thorin. If it weren't for your help, I wouldn't have gotten out in one piece. But I won't waste words thanking you. You and I both know we don't need that between us.

It's already been quite a while since you woke up. So if you're still worrying about what you've forgotten, maybe you don't need to. Even if those memories are gone for good, it's nothing to be sad about. Because as long as you're still here, I'm not going anywhere. Our friendship will keep going. No matter how many times we start over, no matter how long it takes, we'll always have new memories to make.

Of course, I don't mean to suggest you should go and lose your memory again. Please take care of yourself, my dear friend.

I've enclosed a magic rune I came across during my travels. Ever since I learned that mages can <style="highlight">draw rewards</style> from them, I've been setting a few aside for you. Consider it a small gift.

Wishing you a safe journey ahead.

<align="right">Your dear friend,
Hogan

480.title: Valka's Letter
480.content:
<style="stress"><player_name></style>, months have flown by since we parted ways. I hope everything's been well with you.

Winter is approaching here in the Duchy of Whiteridge, and with it, the season of festivities. This year, the people of Cedartown have decided to break with tradition and merge the Snowspire Festival with the <style="highlight">Autumn Harvest</style>, creating one big celebration that honors both the season's bounty and the approach of winter's rest.

This decision makes perfect sense for those of us living in the mountains. Our Fall Harvest was always more about honoring the departed, so combining it with Snowspire creates a celebration that embraces both the joy of harvest and solemn remembrance.

The townsfolk welcomed me, Carolina, Shemira, and the others with open arms. Igor and Daimon delighted the children with their playful antics, and generous dwarven craftsmen provided Callan with tools to fix his machines. Carolina was so grateful for that. Even Ludovic, though he chose not to attend, had his manor adorned with beautiful decorations by his devoted staff, making it feel bright and festive.

But the greatest gift come from you, my friend. Your courage alongside Rodrigo have truly transformed hearts and minds. The people have overcome their ancient fear of the Graveborn. Where once they saw my comrades as Hypogean servants, they now recognize their true nobility. This shift brings me joy beyond measure.

I know your thoughts often turn to Princess Yolena, as do mine. I recently journeyed back to the Petalia Plains, to the place where we said our goodbyes, and prayed for her. I hope with all my heart that she's reached the shimmering sea of her dreams, and discovered the boundless beauty she sought. Wherever she is now, our love and memories will be with her.

Rodrigo, Gerda, and all the Graveborn here in Whiteridge send their greetings. May your travels be safe, and your festivities filled with peace and joy. I've enclosed some <style="highlight">ancient runes</style> that the dwarves recently uncovered. May they <style="highlight">serve you well on your journey.</style>


<align="right">Your steadfast and eternal friend,
<align="right">Valka

481.title: Letter from Ravion
481.content:
<style="stress"><player_name></style>, my friend,

How have you been? You haven't been away from Sal'thorin long, but I already miss having someone around who actually gets my jokes—unlike our stone-faced Indris.

Is life on the surface so great that you've forgotten those of us still underground? Things down here have been... eventful. Indris keeps creating awkward situations that I somehow have to solve. Honestly, working for him isn't any easier than working for my mother! But if it helps my people live more dignified lives, I suppose it's a worthy sacrifice for Sal'thorin.

I'm not writing this letter just to complain, or because I'm bored, or because there's a mountain of paperwork on my desk with some blank paper sitting nearby. I'm writing because I wanted to <style="highlight">thank you</style>. With a friendship like ours, I'm sure you know exactly what I mean.

Oh, and I found something: a curious stone tablet inscribed with a line of <style="highlight">strange runes</style> carved into it. They seem to hold some kind of magical power, and I bet someone as smart as you could figure out how to use them better than I can.

Write back when you get a chance. I want to hear all about your adventures!

<align="right">Your friend,
<align="right">Ravion

482.title: Greetings from Damian!
482.content:
Magister Merlin, the <style="highlight">Winter Carnival</style> is right around the corner. Wishing you joy this festive season!

You won't believe how lively Lunadorf is this time of year! Some of our Wilder kin from underground came up to visit the Dark Forest, and Granny Dahnie prepared a feast so lavish the tables nearly buckled. I ended up pulling out my quickvine conveyor belt so everyone could take turns eating all the delicious dishes. Grandpa Arden said I was brilliant for thinking of it!

Our visitors brought all sorts of fascinating things from underground—strange creatures and plants I'd never seen, plus ingeniously crafted dwarven machines. They're giving me so many incredible ideas. I've already planned out three months' worth of experiments, and when my new invention is done, it will absolutely blow everyone away! I can't wait to share it with you first!

I also found some <style="highlight">strange symbols</style> in the books they brought. They are said to contain powerful magic. I hope they prove useful to you! Wishing you a happy Winter Carnival!

<align="right">Damian

530.title: Greetings from Faramor
530.content:
Dear <style="stress"><player_name></style>,

It has been over a year since we last parted at Whiteridge. Lately, my thoughts have returned more than once to the Snowspire Festival of last year, as though those days were not so distant after all. Time passes quickly. With the arrival of a new year, I imagine Cedartown is already preparing for its festival once again. I find myself wishing I could return, even briefly, to see our friends there.

This past year has kept me constantly on the road. I have continued my search without rest, seldom allowing myself to linger in one place. Yesterday, a sudden snowfall swept through the region, and it was only when I saw people braving the storm to prepare the Emberlight Market that I realized the <style="highlight">Emberlight Festival</style> was close at hand. Since becoming an undead hunter, I have rarely taken part in such celebrations, yet the simple joy people share during festivals has always left a strong impression on me. <style="highlight">Fireworks and a bustling market</style> still have a way of bringing warmth and comfort, no matter how severe the cold.

At times, I find myself wishing I could spend a festival like this in the company of friends, though I have long grown used to traveling alone. Perhaps one day we will meet again and welcome the first light of a new year together.

Enclosed is a small New Year's gift. A few days ago, I came across a <style="highlight">rune</style> in an old handwritten manuscript, one said to carry blessings. I believe it will <style="highlight">be of use to you</style>.

Please accept my New Year's wishes, and extend my regards to those at your side. May the Emberlight Festival bring you warmth, and may the year ahead pass smoothly.

<align="right">Yours sincerely,
<align="right">Faramor

531.title: Neatly Written Letter
531.content:
Dear Magister,

I hope this letter finds you well. These past days at the academy with you have been immensely rewarding for me. In fact, when we met yesterday, I wanted to express my gratitude right then and there, but I was afraid I wouldn't be able to keep my emotions in check and risk exposing your disguise. So instead, I chose to write this letter. I hope you won't mind.

To have you return to the academy, even if not under the name Merlin, was a huge surprise. Ever since I first came to the Lyceum, I've often dreamed of being one of your students who gets to learn from you about magic and life itself. Now that this dream has finally come true, nothing could make me happier or more worthy of celebration.

I'm sitting at my desk as I write this, but a tantalizing scent keeps slipping in through the crack under the door, and my thoughts have already drifted from my books to the kitchen. I can tell Father is making his specialty stew, and Mother must have all the ingredients ready for her little puddings. The dining table is probably covered with its embroidered tablecloth by now, set neatly with our finest silverware and candleholders. Everyone in my family is looking forward to tonight's dinner. Father says today is a good day, one for family, surrounded by warmth, happiness, and good food.

Magister Merlin, I only wish you could be here as well. I hesitated again and again yesterday, and in the end I couldn't bring myself to invite you over. I regret it a little now. I'll gather my courage and ask properly next time, so you can enjoy the dishes my parents are proud of.

 My family and I wish you every success in your work here at the academy. May you always be happy and always blessed.

<align="right">With respect and gratitude,
<align="right">Cassadee

532.title: Card from the Library
532.content:
Little Merlin,

It has been dreadfully dull these days. Little Leymar is gone. Neither you nor Little Zorya shows up at the library now. There is no one to play chess with, and no one to chat with! So I have had to entertain myself the only way I can: keeping a close eye on the students, seeing who is breaking the rules. If, lately, the rules feel a little more... unforgiving, don't blame me. That's what you get when all a librarian does is work with no fun at all.

Speaking of which, I have noticed something interesting. There have been more and more students romancing in the library lately. Yesterday alone, there were twelve couples making eyes at each other, whispering behind their books, blushing, hearts practically racing out of their chests. Honestly. Why do they insist on meeting in a library, of all places—surrounded by knowledge and regulations? Would strolling hand-in-hand through the art gallery or the market street really cool down their feelings?

Well, of course, I know <style="highlight">Valentine's Day</style> is approaching, so in the end, I punished only the pair who decided to confess their love right here in the library. The others who did not cause real trouble, I let them go! See? Gentle. Adorable. Considerate. That is me. So tell me: when you have a Hypogean this kind, do you not feel even the tiniest urge to grant me a long holiday? A little mercy, perhaps?

Ah, I hear the bell! Closing time! I am off the clock at last! That is enough writing. Rest time is sacred, and work should not be allowed to steal the happiest hours of the day.

Depths take me, Merlin. You should rest as well. Do not forget what I told you: proper rest and sleep are especially important for someone with amnesia!

P.S. There's a gift tucked inside! Just take it!

<align="right">Yours, in need of a vacation
<align="right">Contess

533.title: Greetings from Solise
533.content:
Dear <style="stress"><player_name></style>,

You may be surprised to receive a letter from me. After all, we're all in here, the Serene Lyceum. We have plenty of chances to meet and talk. Still, I find that putting thoughts to paper invites a quieter kind of care. It's more considered, more heartfelt.

Spring has arrived, and with it the <style="highlight">Dawnlight Revelry</style>. Around this season, even the magical plants on campus seem a little more lively than usual. I've noticed many students brimming with bright ideas. Some have even combined magic with music, preparing performances that promise to be truly one of a kind. If you're willing, I hope you'll indulge their wonderful creativity and spend a little of this joyful season with them.

In the Lyceum, many of our young ones look up to you with admiration. They speak of your journey with relish, holding you up as both a role model and a legend. Birds yet to take flight are always like this. They yearn for the world beyond, whether it brings fair winds or storm. I am proud of them, yet I cannot help but worry.And so, I have a somewhat presumptuous request. When you find the time, would you consider giving a public lecture here in the Lyceum? Your experience and insight may well be more valuable than anything found in the library.

The Dawnlight Revelry is just around the corner. I've prepared some festive gifts for you, and I hope you won't turn them away. I would be truly glad if they could be of even a little use to you.
 
May your heart be at peace, and your health endure.
<align="right">Best wishes,
<align="right">Solise

547.title: Letter With Lyceum Crest
547.content:
Dear Magister Merlin,

Hope you're doing well! I haven't seen much of you on campus lately. Will you be sticking around for a while? No rush to reply—just whenever you get the chance.

For me, life has gone on as usual since the selection exam... My routine remains much the same, and yet, something feels different. For a time, my thoughts kept drifting back to Headmaster Leymar, Cyran, and... Gervan. The fierce, mocking look in his eyes when he turned into a Hypofiend haunted me, even in my sleep. Not knowing what else to do, I turned to Professor Solise for help.

Her prescription for me was simple: "Keep yourself busy." Taking her advice, I've spent almost all my free time doing volunteer work around campus. I polished every display case in the museum, tended the rare plants in the Grove Academy, helped Liam organize the storage room, and even repaired a pile of broken crucibles... I've been as busy as a bee, and it's actually working—I've been sleeping much better. Pippa says I'm simply exhausted, but who can say? Maybe labor really does have a therapeutic effect.

Besides volunteering, I've been practicing with the new Oath of Glory you gave me. It feels a bit different from the old one, probably because of the materials. I'll need a little more time to get used to it before I can handle it as well as before.

Once again, I'd like to express my sincerest thanks. I still have much to learn and many challenges ahead of me, but I'll always remember my pledge: should you ever need me, the Oath of Glory will rise for you!

Ah, this letter has turned out much longer than I expected—my apologies. If you'll be around campus a while longer, I'd love the chance to visit you at the Stellar Spire. There are many things I'd like to ask you.

May your wisdom continue to guide me like the eternal stars.

<align="right">Your friend and knight,
<align="right">Silven Grenvalden

548.title: Zorya's Letter
548.content:
Dear Merlin,

With peace restored at the Lyceum, I imagine your next journey is already on the horizon.

As a professor of the Lyceum, I ought to insist that you fulfill your duties and make up for your absence over the past two decades. However, I am also Bedivere, and I know well that you bear far greater responsibilities, and that the Lyceum cannot keep you here for long. The best solution, then, is to have you pay the penalty stipulated in your employment contract.

Revealing your identity as Merlin is akin to placing yourself at the very center of a storm. From now on, your every move will be under scrutiny. You will face praise and criticism alike, along with doubt, probing, and attack. Be mindful of those around you: some may wish you well, while others may harbor ill intent. As your professor, I know you possess the wit and insight to overcome whatever trials lie ahead. Even so, I must remind you to stay prepared and give your all. Pay no heed to the opinions and judgments of others, just as you did when you skipped classes back then.

Now that you have taken center stage, there is no need to hesitate or hold back. Merlin was always meant to shine.

The path ahead is bound to be perilous. Please take care of yourself, and do not risk your safety unless it is truly necessary.

I will remain at the Lyceum and carry out my duties as Bedivere. If you ever need my help, I will be there.

P.S. You forgot to tell me what your two familiars like to eat. Be sure to let me know in your reply.

<align="right">Your professor and companion,
<align="right">Zorya

549.title: Paper Boat Letter
549.content:

<style="stress"><player_name></style>, when are you coming back? I miss hanging out with you!

Whiteridge's the best place in the world! It's always snowing, and there are cemeteries for me to explore. I've met so many friends to go to the festival with! Hee-hee—I gave a lot of people a good scare this year, and I loved hearing them scream. I also enjoy playing hide-and-seek with Alex, Albina, Orla, and Daimon in Cedartown! But Shemira's turned into a bore and doesn't want to spar with me anymore. What a shame.

Valka said you've been very busy... Hmm, is it because Children's Day is coming up, and you've been off having fun? If so, you should come find me! There's so much we can do, like tombstone hopping, snowball fights, hide-and-seek, or even sparring! Your call!

Oh, and guess what? Daimon taught me how to make paper boats! It's simple, but really fun. Come play with me, and I'll teach you!

(The passage below is written in elegant cursive)

I hope you're doing fine, <style="stress"><player_name></style>. Lately, Igor's been going on and on about wanting to spend time with his "favorite playmate". Since you haven't been around, Valka suggested he write you a letter instead. It took him two whole days just to finish the passage above, but it turned out quite well, don't you think? Writing it gave him a real sense of achievement, and Valka decided to keep him busy with writing lessons whenever he gets bored.

All is well here in Whiteridge. Although the royal court has yet to appoint a new Archduke, Rodrigo's been doing an excellent job holding things together. I heard you've been to many fascinating places and met lots of new friends. Do come back and visit when you have the time. We'd love to hear all about your adventures.

By the way, I found this <style="highlight">secret glyph</style> in one of the books in my family's collection. I hope it proves useful.

May Dura bless your journey ahead.

<align="right">Igor and Carolina

550.title: Sun-Kissed Letter
550.content:
<style="stress"><player_name></style>, I'm drying sunflowers in Skyrealm Forest as I write this letter. The weather today is so pleasant, and the warm breeze brushing against my face almost lulled me to sleep. Almost, that is. With three little ones clamoring to be fed at my side, falling asleep is out of the question.

Just the other day, some students slipped up while practicing transfiguration, leaving three baby owls with stubborn traces of magic. Their parents were frightened and ended up abandoning the poor things. As you can imagine, I'm now busy taking care of the trio. Much as I believe in not interfering with nature, as their professor, I have to help clean up my students' mess, don't I?

The three little fluff balls seem to have taken me for their father. They follow me everywhere, mimicking my every move. The trouble is, I'm an expert in transfiguration, not in raising animals... I'm still not quite sure how to teach them to fly or survive. Hmm, maybe I should start appearing as an owlbear before them? That would probably make them feel more at ease.

You may not realize it yet, but ever since you helped the animals here resolve their troubles, you've become someone they deeply revere. So far, six animals (including animal spirits) have asked me to pass along their regards to you, each bringing a gift—a bone treasured by a puppy, bugs caught by a kitten, a glass marble cherished by a crow, and a molted tail feather from a parrot. Heh, I've thanked them on your behalf. Knowing you'd prefer they keep their beloved possessions, I persuaded them to take their gifts back, save for <style="highlight">a stone engraved with ancient script</style>. I hope you don't mind. Here's the inscription. It may come in handy along the way.

<style="stress"><player_name></style>, I hear you'll be leaving the Lyceum soon. I must admit I'm a little disappointed, as I had thought you might stay and teach here. Whenever you feel the need for a respite from your journey, do come back for a cup of tea and help me with my dried sunflowers.

<align="right">Your owl-keeper friend,
<align="right">Hepler

576.title: Letter Bearing the Royal Seal
576.content:
Dear <style="stress"><player_name></style>,
How's everything on your end?
Savannah's been hit with merciless heat waves lately. Once the sun goes down, the central plaza fills with people out to enjoy the cool evening air. The bazaar stays open well into the night, with stalls selling all sorts of lovely handicrafts like woven bracelets, beautiful lanterns, and lifelike fox figurines. They're obviously modeled after King Rolan in his fox form!

I was tempted to get one the other day, but then I hesitated... would it be disrespectful to King Rolan? What do you think? If you say it's fine, I'll definitely get one!

Rowan went with me that day, but I could tell he was really there to scout new ideas for his Secret Pals Boxes! Hmph! Can't he stop thinking about business for even a second when we're out together? I couldn't take it anymore, so I ordered him to forget about work and enjoy the bazaar with me!

Later, we stopped by a ring toss stall, and it was fun! Rowan went on and on about how good he was at judging distance and angles... then missed his very first throw! Sure, he won a few small prizes afterward, but I bet the stall owner went easy on him just because he's the Mithril Consortium young master! It's not like I lost to him or anything!

Oh, I almost forgot to tell you about the pretty star lamp I found at the bazaar! It's painted with two stars, facing each other. When the lamp is lit, their shadows overlap, as if they've crossed paths in the night sky. I love it so much that I've put it on my bedside table. I'll show it to you next time we meet!

Most importantly, I got you a rare magical tome from a traveling merchant. He claimed it contains amazing spells that only a true mage can understand. If you use them the right way, you'll even <style="highlight">earn rewards</style>! I couldn't make much sense of it myself, but I'm sure you'll know what to do with it!

May the stars shine bright over your city tonight!

Ah, I've gone on for far too long. Don't make fun of me for rambling!

<align="right">Peggy

577.title: Letter with Orange Fox Fur
577.content:
(The top of the letter bears a messy fox paw print)
Hey, hero of Savannah.

Getting any downtime lately? As for me, I've been kept on my toes! Most of my days are spent dodging my overzealous admirers. They've even formed a fan club called the "Team King Rolan"! I honestly don't know how anyone says that cringeworthy name with a straight face. Every time I hear it, my tail puffs up from sheer secondhand embarrassment.

Sadly, Savannah isn't nearly as fox-friendly as it used to be. Stalls selling fox merchandise are everywhere, and people go wild the moment they spot an unsuspecting fox on the streets, convinced it might be me. Some have even resorted to luring me out with roast chicken... And while I do enjoy free food, this is getting a little out of hand.

Still... it's nice to see the children running around the streets again, carefree as ever. They're a noisy bunch, but they often bring odd little knickknacks to my den as offerings. I suppose I can forgive them for that.

Yesterday evening, I enjoyed a little peace and quiet on the highest rooftop of the palace. (Don't ask how I got up there—I have my ways.) The sun had left the roof tiles pleasantly warm beneath me, and from up there I could take in all of Savannah at a glance. A cheering crowd filled the open-air theater. At Bell Bazaar, a stingy stall owner haggled at the top of his lungs with a customer. Down at the docks, the workers were as busy as ever. The city was at peace. It's hard to believe it was once reduced to ruins by war, so many years ago.

Come to think of it, humans are remarkably easy to satisfy. Give them enough to eat, clothes to wear, and a place where they can live in peace, and they'll be smiling from ear to ear. More often than not, happiness is found in simple things like these, and they're worth fighting tooth and nail to protect.

Ah, forgive me for getting a little carried away. Anyway, now that Savannah is safe again, don't you think it's about time you kept your end of our deal? I did you a huge favor by showing you around last time you were here. Surely treating me to a meal isn't too much to ask of the great Magister Merlin, is it?

If you're not sure what I like... you can't go wrong with the grilled fish from the Rusty Barrel Tavern. Just tell them to slather it in extra honey! See? I've already made this easy for you.

By the way, I found a rune among my offerings. Not much good to a fox like me, but I hear mages can <style="highlight">get rewards</style> from it. Now, that's all the more reason you should get me that grilled fish!

<align="right">Your thoughtful fox friend, Rolan

578.title: Letter With Raven Feathers
578.content:
Dear Magister Merlin,

Tonight, the moon is nothing short of enchanting, and its beauty mesmerizes me.

This may be a rather clichéd way to begin a letter, but trust me, I'm not trying to sound like a poet. As a vampire, it'd be unbecoming of me to sing the praises of the sun or a crackling fire.

Magister, have you ever wandered through Savannah after nightfall? When the silvery moon hangs overhead, things that usually go unnoticed during the day reveal themselves—from love letters tucked into sleeves to shady deals struck under the table by unscrupulous politicians.

Anywhere beneath the moon is a perfect spot for a romantic rendezvous or an illicit deal. The sight of the moon sometimes reminds one of their homeland, or of the hardships they've been through. The moon treats everyone the same, casting the same pale light over every one of them.

Isn't it fascinating? That's exactly what draws me to the moon.

It lends a little color to my long and tedious life.

You know, I'm usually not one to give out information for free, but tonight's an exception. Maybe the moonlight struck a chord in me, or maybe I just want to do something to shatter the boredom of these peaceful days in Savannah. Whatever the reason, I'm in the mood to send you a gift.

I've enclosed a rune with this letter. I'm certain you can unravel its secrets and reap a generous <style="highlight">reward</style> from it. Its origin, however, is a tale best left untold. After all, once a secret has been laid bare, it loses both its allure and its worth.

I hope the same moon is watching over you tonight.

<align="right">Eryndor
